extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants, patent practitioners, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality standards (MPEP §608.02 and 37 C.F.R. 1.81/1.84) for preparing, submitting, labeling, and amending drawings and photographs in U.S. patent applications, including when drawings are required and how post-filing drawings are treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a drawing must be furnished (35 U.S.C. 113; 37 C.F.R. 1.81)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall furnish a drawing where necessary for the understanding of the subject matter to be patented. The applicant for a patent is required to furnish a drawing of the invention where necessary for the understanding of the subject matter sought to be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the nature of the subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing and no drawing was furnished, the Commissioner/Examiner may require submission within not less than two months from notice. Original drawings should be retained by applicant for future correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on drawings submitted after the filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings submitted after the filing date of the application may not be used (i) to overcome any insufficiency of the specification due to lack of an enabling disclosure or otherwise inadequate disclosure therein, or (ii) to supplement the original disclosure thereof for the purpose of interpretation of the scope of any claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute or additional drawing that introduces new matter should not be entered; the examiner should describe the new matter in the next Office action. Entry decisions are reviewable by petition (37 CFR 1.181).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date rules regarding absence of drawings (post- and pre- Dec 18, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after December 18, 2013 (other than design applications), 35 U.S.C. 111 no longer requires a drawing to obtain a filing date, but 35 U.S.C. 113 still requires drawings when necessary. For applications filed before December 18, 2013, a drawing (where necessary) or a high quality copy must be filed with the application to be entitled to a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications (35 U.S.C. 171) must be filed with required drawings to get a filing date regardless of filing date. Inclusion of drawings at filing is prudent to avoid statutory defects such as lack of enablement or new matter issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP initial determination of whether drawings are 'necessary'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP) will make the initial decision in all new applications as to whether a drawing is 'necessary' under the first sentence of 35 U.S.C. 113.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A drawing is considered necessary where the drawing is referred to in the specification and one or more figures have been omitted. If drawings are required and not included, OPAP informs applicant; for pre-2013 filings lack of required drawings can render the application incomplete and delay a filing date. If an examiner determines a filing date should not have been granted for lack of drawings (pre-2013), the SPE should review and may request cancellation of the filing date with a memorandum identifying required subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: When subject matter 'admits of illustration' (second sentence of 35 U.S.C. 113) — examiner requirement and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 113 second sentence applies where a drawing is not necessary but the subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing and no drawing was submitted; this is treated as an informality and the examiner may require a drawing under 37 CFR 1.81(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should require at least an ink sketch or permanent print in the applicant's next reply to the requirement to permit early sufficiency review and to prevent new matter. Use form paragraph 6.23 or 6.23.01. Applicant is given at least two months to submit drawings; form paragraph 6.23.01 may set a shortened statutory TWO (2) MONTHS with possible extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) but cannot exceed six months overall. Failure to timely submit a required drawing can result in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and treatment of substitute or additional drawings discovered to contain new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner discovers new matter in a substitute or additional drawing, the drawing should not be entered and the examiner should describe the new matter that resulted in non-entry in the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new drawing without new matter may be required if the examiner determines a drawing is needed under 37 CFR 1.81 or 1.83. Form paragraph 6.37 may be used. Applicant may petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to review the examiner’s decision not to enter a drawing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable drawing categories — black ink and color rules (37 C.F.R. 1.84(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Two acceptable categories for presenting drawings: (1) Black ink—black and white drawings normally required using India ink or equivalent solid black lines; or (2) Color—color drawings permitted in design applications, and only permitted in utility applications on rare occasions upon grant of a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings for utility applications require petition with fee (37 CFR 1.17(h)), one set if e-filed (three sets if paper), and an amendment to the specification inserting prescribed language in the Brief Description of the Drawings. Color drawings must be of sufficient quality so all details are reproducible in black and white. Color drawings are not permitted in international applications (PCT Rule 11.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs — when allowed and quality requirements (37 C.F.R. 1.84(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs are not ordinarily permitted in utility and design patent applications, but will be accepted if photographs are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention (e.g., electrophoresis gels, blots, micrographs, animals, plants, ornamental effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs must be of sufficient quality so that all details are reproducible in the printed patent. If the subject admits of illustration by a drawing, the examiner may require a drawing instead. Color photographs have the same petition/quality requirements as color drawings for utility applications; in lieu of ink drawings there is no petition required but the photographs must comply with 37 CFR 1.84(b)(1). Only one set of photographs is required when submitted in lieu of ink drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of drawing sheets and labeling of post-filing sheets (37 C.F.R. 1.84(c); 37 C.F.R. 1.121(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia (title, inventor’s name, application or docket number if assigned) should be placed on the front of each sheet within the top margin. Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date must be labeled in the top margin as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet'. Marked-up copies must be labeled 'Annotated Sheet'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If provided, identification must be on the front of each sheet within the top margin. Labeling lets the Office recognize how to treat entry of the sheet. Corrections to drawings must be made by replacement sheets labeled 'Replacement Sheet' because the Office does not release drawings for direct correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms in drawings — formulas, tables, waveforms (37 C.F.R. 1.84(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings and are subject to the same requirements as drawings. Each chemical or mathematical formula must be labeled as a separate figure; groups of waveforms must be presented as a single figure using a common vertical axis with time along the horizontal axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each individual waveform discussed in the specification must be identified with a separate letter designation adjacent to the vertical axis. Use brackets when necessary to indicate integration of formula material into figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper quality and single-sided requirement (37 C.F.R. 1.84(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be made on paper which is flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny, and durable. Only one side of the sheet may be used for the drawing. Sheets must be reasonably free from cracks, creases, folds, erasures, alterations, overwritings, and interlineations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs must be developed on paper meeting sheet-size and margin requirements. Black and white drawings submitted after filing may be transmitted by facsimile if quality is not unreasonably degraded; color drawings cannot be faxed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing sheet size uniformity and acceptable sizes (37 C.F.R. 1.84(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawing sheets in an application must be the same size. Acceptable sizes are 21.0 cm by 29.7 cm (DIN A4) or 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm (8 1/2 by 11 inches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is required that all drawing sheets in a particular application be the same size for ease of handling. See MPEP § 608.01 for certified copies of application-as-filed that do not meet sheet size/margin and quality requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins and sight area (37 C.F.R. 1.84(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: No frames around the sight; sight should include scan target points on two cater-corner margin corners. Required margins: top at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), left at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), right at least 1.5 cm (5/8 inch), bottom at least 1.0 cm (3/8 inch), yielding sight limits specific to the sheet size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheets must not contain frames around the usable surface. The sight sizes are identified specifically for A4 and 8.5 x 11 sheets. Drawing sheets should be free of extraneous marks in margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views — general requirements and placement (37 C.F.R. 1.84(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing must contain as many views as necessary to show the invention. Views may be plan, elevation, section, or perspective; detail views may be used. All views must be grouped together and arranged on the sheet(s) without wasting space, preferably in an upright position, clearly separated from one another, and must not be included in the sheets containing the specifications, claims, or abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Views must not be connected by projection lines and must not contain center lines. Waveforms may be connected by dashed lines to show timing. Views on multiple sheets that form a single complete view must be assemblable without concealing any part of the views on the various sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploded, partial, sectional, alternate-position and modified-form view rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploded views are permissible and when shown with another figure on the same sheet should be bracketed. Partial views may be used and if a large machine is broken into partial views they must be capable of being linked edge to edge; include a smaller scale view showing the whole. Sectional views must indicate the plane on the view from which section is cut and use hatching to indicate cross sections. A moved (alternate) position may be shown by a broken line; modified forms of construction must be shown in separate views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hatching must be regularly spaced oblique parallel lines (preferably 45°) and not impede reference characters; different parts should be hatched consistently; juxtaposed elements should have different hatch angles. When a partial view is enlarged, both the partial and enlarged view must be labeled as separate views. Very long views may be divided but the relationship must be unambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and orientation of views on sheets (37 C.F.R. 1.84(h)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: One view must not be placed upon another or within the outline of another. All views on the same sheet should stand in the same direction and be readable with the sheet held upright; if wider views require turning the sheet on its side, words must still appear left-to-right when upright or when top becomes right side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If views wider than the sheet are necessary, the sheet may be turned so the top is on the right-hand side; graphs using normal axis conventions are an exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page view suitability (37 C.F.R. 1.84(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the views should be suitable for inclusion on the front page of the patent application publication and patent as the illustration of the invention. Applicant may suggest a single view (by figure number) for front page inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Views must not contain projection lines or center lines. The suggested front-page view should clearly show the invention for publication purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale limitations (37 C.F.R. 1.84(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: The scale to which a drawing is made must be large enough to show the mechanism without crowding when the drawing is reduced in size to two-thirds in reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications such as 'actual size' or 'scale 1/2' are not permitted because they lose meaning with reproduction in different formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of lines, numbers, and letters (37 C.F.R. 1.84(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawings must be made by a process which will give satisfactory reproduction characteristics. Every line, number, and letter must be durable, clean, black (except for color drawings), sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight of lines/letters must permit adequate reproduction including fine lines and shading. Different thicknesses may be used when differences have distinct meaning; applies to all lines including those representing cut surfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading standards (37 C.F.R. 1.84(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: Shading is encouraged if it aids understanding and does not reduce legibility; shading indicates surface or shape of spherical, cylindrical, and conical elements; flat parts may be lightly shaded; shading preferred in perspective views but not for cross sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use spaced thin lines, as few as practicable, contrasting with the rest of the drawing. As a substitute, heavy lines on the shade side can be used if they do not superimpose or obscure reference characters. Light should come from the upper left at 45°. Solid black shading areas are not permitted except for bar graphs or color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of symbols in drawings (37 C.F.R. 1.84(n))
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical drawing symbols may be used for conventional elements when appropriate and should be adequately identified in the specification. ANSI and ISO publications are considered generally acceptable guides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not 'approve' an entire published collection of symbols as a group; use is decided case-by-case. Avoid overly specific symbols; label unclear symbols for clarification. In design patents, symbols should be used judiciously as they may interfere with showing the appearance; color may be preferred for design features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legends (37 C.F.R. 1.84(o))
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitable descriptive legends may be used subject to approval by the Office, or required by the examiner where necessary for understanding of the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legends should contain as few words as possible and only where necessary for comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference characters, numerals, letters rules (37 C.F.R. 1.84(p))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters (numerals preferred), sheet numbers, and view numbers must be plain and legible, not used with brackets or inverted commas or enclosed outlines, and oriented in the same direction as the view. The English alphabet must be used for letters except where another alphabet is customarily used. Reference characters must measure at least .32 cm (1/8 inch) in height.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference characters should follow the profile of the object, not cross or mingle with lines, and should not be placed on hatched/shaded surfaces (underlining may be used where necessary). The same part across multiple views must use the same reference character; the same character must never designate different parts. Reference characters not mentioned in the description shall not appear in the drawings; those mentioned must appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead line requirements (37 C.F.R. 1.84(q))
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead lines (lines between reference characters and the details referred to) may be straight or curved and should be as short as possible, originating in immediate proximity to the reference character and extending to the indicated feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead lines must not cross each other, must be executed in the same way as other lines in the drawing, and are required for each reference character except those indicating the surface or cross section where the reference character must be underlined to show the absence of a lead line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of arrows in drawings (37 C.F.R. 1.84(r))
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrows may be used at ends of lines provided their meaning is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted uses include (1) freestanding arrow on a lead line to indicate an entire section, (2) an arrow touching a line to indicate the surface shown by the line looking along the arrow direction, and (3) to show direction of movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright or mask work notice placement and content (37 C.F.R. 1.84(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may appear in the drawing but must be placed within the sight immediately below the figure representing the copyrighted or mask work material and be limited to letters .32 to .64 cm (1/8 to 1/4 inches) high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The content of the notice must be limited to only elements provided by law (e.g., '©1983 John Doe'). Inclusion is permitted only if authorization language set forth in 37 CFR 1.71(e) is included at the beginning of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of drawing sheets (37 C.F.R. 1.84(t))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets of drawings should be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1 within the sight; numbers must be placed in the middle of the top of the sheet (but not in the margin) or on the right-hand side if drawing extends too close to the middle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheet numbering must be clear and larger than reference character numbers. The number of each sheet should be shown as 'current_sheet/total_sheets' using two Arabic numerals separated by an oblique line, with no other marking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of views (37 C.F.R. 1.84(u))
rubrics_metrics.description: Different views must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1, independent of sheet numbering, and in the order they appear on the drawing sheets if possible. Partial views intended to form one complete view must be identified by the same number followed by a capital letter. View numbers must be preceded by the abbreviation 'FIG.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where only a single view is used it must not be numbered and the abbreviation 'FIG.' must not appear. Numbers and letters identifying views must be simple and clear and larger than the numbers used for reference characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security markings placement (37 C.F.R. 1.84(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized security markings may be placed on the drawings provided they are outside the sight, preferably centered in the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security markings must not interfere with the usable sight area of the drawing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections to drawings — durability and replacement sheets (37 C.F.R. 1.84(w); 37 C.F.R. 1.121(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any corrections on drawings submitted to the Office must be durable and permanent. Corrections to drawings must be made by replacement sheets labeled in the header 'Replacement Sheet' since the Office does not release drawings for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a marked-up copy of an amended drawing figure including annotations is filed, such marked-up copy must be labeled 'Annotated Sheet'. Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date must be identified as 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet'.

rubrics_metrics.name: No holes or other physical modifications to drawing sheets (37 C.F.R. 1.84(x))
rubrics_metrics.description: No holes should be made by applicant in the drawing sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid any physical modifications (holes, staples, etc.) that could interfere with processing or reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of drawings and references for specialized drawings (37 C.F.R. 1.84(y) and cross-references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different rules apply to specific types of drawings (design drawings, international design reproductions, plant drawings, reissue drawings). See referenced sections (§ 1.152 for design, § 1.1026 for international design, § 1.165 for plant, § 1.173(a)(2) for reissue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good quality copies are acceptable if lines are uniformly thick, black, and solid. See cited MPEP sections for detailed requirements for each drawing type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawing/photograph petition handling and storage (policy/guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings and color photographs are permitted in design applications without petition; for utility applications color requires a petition and fee and must meet quality and specification-amendment requirements. Color drawings/photographs are not permitted in international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include fee, correct number of sets (1 if e-filed, 3 if paper), and amend specification to include prescribed language. If color drawings or photographs are filed in a continuing utility application, applicant must renew the petition even if a similar petition was granted in the prior application. Color items are stored in a content management system and a black-and-white copy placed in the file wrapper with a placeholder sheet. Utility egrants after April 18, 2023 may include color; printed patents historically reproduced only in black and white.
